answer: Proof-of-space-time resists sybils by making each identity pledge a distinct, unforgeable region of physical disk. A node commits a large unique dataset, like a walnut shell packed with randomized grains, then answers surprise audits proving it still holds every byte. Shared storage fails the checks, so N fake identities demand N times the real capacity: the cost climbs like a summit route with no shortcut, every forged peer another ledge the attacker must physically carve and keep provisioned.
